The greenhouse effect is a natural process [1] that benefits humanity [1]. It leads to the
presence of greenhouse gases such as water vapour, carbon dioxide and methane in the
atmosphere [1]. These allow incoming short-wave radiation to pass through and reach the
Earth, but they trap a proportion of the outgoing long-wave radiation. This raises the
temperature of the atmosphere [1]. As a result, the Earth is about 30°C warmer than it would
be if there were no greenhouse gases, and this allows humans to survive on Earth [1]. Global
warming is the increase in temperature of the Earth [1] as a result of increased amounts of
greenhouse gases in the Earth’s atmosphere [1]. These increased amounts of greenhouse
gases are causing global warming, which is dangerous for people [1].                   [Max 4 marks]

Climate change mitigation means preventing global climate change [1]. Global climate
change adaptation means adapting to global climate change, in other words learning to
live with it rather than preventing it [1].
[Max 2 marks]

Answers are likely to distinguish between mitigation (trying to prevent climate
change) and adaptation (learning to live with climate change). Mitigation is better
than adaptation in the long term, as adaptation will not prevent climate change.
However, the impacts of climate change may occur all over the world and not just
in the countries that are causing global climate change. Answers may evaluate
techniques such as afforestation, using electric vehicles, building higher flood protection
schemes, drought-resistant crops, desalination plants, making more anti-malarial drugs
available, geoengineering schemes, etc. Answers may also consider the trends in climate
change – the impacts of climate change will differ depending on whether temperatures
rise by 1.5°C, 2°C or 4°C, for example. There must be some evaluation of specific
techniques/strategies. For answers that consider only mitigation or adaptation, do not
award more than 5 marks.
[Max 7 marks]
